note: ⌨️ The keyboard path of every generation3d editor verb a user repeats. It lists the chords THIS APP declares; the framework mints its own on top (`undo`/`redo` appear here because the app re-declares them, while the interaction domain's `escape`→`clearSelection` and `mod+a`→`selectAll` are minted by `build_definition` and are deliberately NOT this fixture's to state). A chord here MUST reach an ARG-FREE declared action: `ShellHost`'s keybinding loop fires an arg-free action straight through `onAction`, and opens a staged argument form for anything else — which is slower than the control the chord was meant to replace. A chord for a WINDOW-OWNED action (`windowScoped`, with `ownerWindowKindId` naming the kind whose `window_kind_action_refs` declares it) reaches THAT window whenever the active mode mounts it, focused or not, and is a hinted no-operation in a mode that mounts no owner — never a dead key (`🏛️ShellHost/⌨️window-scope/🟦️.ts`, ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END). A chord token is matched against `event.key` verbatim, so punctuation is spelled as the character (`.`), never as a name (`period`). Both measured against the running playground, not inferred. `fitGraph` is deliberately absent: it is shell chrome over the node-graph surface, not an app action, and the shell binds `F` to it itself. Driven by `✏️editor/🧪️tests/🔬️unit/🦀️.rs` `the_editor_binds_every_keyboard_verb_the_fixture_names`; this file, not that test, is the statement.

bindings.why: History — the framework's own reserved verb.
History — the framework's own reserved verb.
Graph — remove what is selected, the chord three sibling artifacts already declare.

Preview — stop a running evaluation. FRAMEWORK-minted: declaring the `previewEval` tool run makes `build_definition` inject the seven `toolRun*` actions onto every window kind and a chord for each that carries one, so the abort reaches whichever window is active. The token is `.` and not `period` because ShellHost matches the last chord segment against event.key verbatim.
Preview — step the shading ladder without reaching for the picker.

Generate — add a generation, the mode's primary create verb. Window-scoped to the Generations window, which only the GENERATE mode mounts: the chord reaches that window there without the user clicking it first, and raises the unowned hint in edit mode. Measured dead in BOTH modes before that (`invoked: []` app-untouched and again with the flow window active).

Graph — the next node in reading order. A BARE arrow because `role="application"`, which the node-graph canvas now carries, is the ARIA contract for `this widget handles its own arrow keys`; window-scoped to the Flow window, which is what keeps a bare arrow out of every other window. The token is the DOM `event.key` lowercased (`arrowdown`), because the chord matcher compares it verbatim.
Graph — the previous node in reading order.
Graph — follows a wire INTO the anchor node.
Graph — follows a wire OUT of the anchor node.
IO — the chord every application in the world uses to open a file.
IO — export; carries a required format, so this chord opens the staged form on purpose.

shellChrome.why: Painted by the shell over any node-graph surface, not declared by this app — the app must NOT re-bind it.

surfaceBindings.why: ⏎️ Enter/Space on the FOCUSED node-graph canvas opens the selected node's ports. Deliberately a surface binding and not a row of `bindings` above: `SurfaceAccessibilityShell` fires an `activate` trigger only for the canvas that actually has focus and calls `preventDefault`, whereas an `enter` chord in the app keybinding table would also fire on every focused button in the shell. `shortcut` is what reaches a screen reader as `aria-keyshortcuts`.
